bug_semantics: The authenticated Alertmanager and Prometheus proxy controllers called skip_forgery_protection while forwarding the browser-controlled method, path, query, and (for Alertmanager) body to their upstream services. A cross-site page could therefore cause a logged-in browser to send its ambient Upright session to a proxy action and reach an enabled upstream write or management endpoint, including Alertmanager silence creation or Prometheus /-/reload, without a Rails authenticity token or an equivalent provenance check.
flaw_origin: The vulnerable proxy implementation originated before the available public Git history. Public commit dbf67daef2c624c1d5f01ef4233a8bccb3c927aa added both already-vulnerable controllers in a commit explicitly titled 'Move UI and Traceroute probe to engine'; the repository itself begins with an 'Initial extraction', and the project's first-party launch article says Upright started as an internal tool. Because a move is not a BIC, the commit that originally chose skip_forgery_protection for session-authenticated, general-purpose upstream proxies is not present in this clone.
ai_marker: unavailable (not absent): the original BIC commit object is outside the public basecamp/upright history, so its author, committer, and trailers cannot be inspected; no AI judgment is inferred from the later extraction/move commit
evidence: Advisory: https://api.github.com/advisories/GHSA-Q9R6-H8CX-Q7QP and https://gist.github.com/Zykis1024/cec690012eecac53f408e78d2b569f06 identify app/controllers/upright/alertmanager_proxy_controller.rb:2 and app/controllers/upright/prometheus_proxy_controller.rb:2 at efe4f2e5254ac6e57e45d2261804cca74dbbca3f; both files contain skip_forgery_protection and proxy arbitrary upstream paths/methods, with the Alertmanager action forwarding request.body. Origin trace: git log -L '/skip_forgery_protection/',+1 on each file at the advisory snapshot reaches 29b423ea9e0cec753da97105afccf7a694a5b0e6 ('Continue extraction of Upright core', a namespace-only rewrite) and then dbf67daef2c624c1d5f01ef4233a8bccb3c927aa ('Move UI and Traceroute probe to engine'), where both files appear from /dev/null already containing the skip and forwarding mechanism. Direct parent-tree check shows dbf67daef2c624c1d5f01ef4233a8bccb3c927aa^ is 2a7dfaf0f5411a0195d11c426aeeab8f34a70211 and git ls-tree -r of that parent has neither proxy controller; this proves absence in the public parent but does not make a stated move the original BIC. git rev-list --max-parents=0 yields 7b400a7d44db470a00634e950012af3157ab0795, titled 'Initial extraction'. The first-party article https://dev.37signals.com/introducing-upright/ states that Upright started as an internal tool before it was open-sourced, corroborating the missing pre-extraction lineage. Fix lifecycle: af938dd148c3fa8d148c51fb664f4e34e6a8ef42 first added the CVE-specific Fetch-Metadata/Origin gate; c53258998efee82d69e64237ba7e362c4160a1c4 made missing provenance fail closed; subsequent review hardened the same-origin rule; d94dedb56cec78461cd14113c337034734813d58 removed skip_forgery_protection and retained Rails verification by overriding verified_request? only for a valid token, bearer token, or accepted same-origin provenance. The relevant controller/concern trees at d94dedb56cec78461cd14113c337034734813d58 and PR merge 997009a6778687ac8c1f0833f2850ea808742cce are identical; merge-base checks place d94dedb56cec78461cd14113c337034734813d58 in 997009a6778687ac8c1f0833f2850ea808742cce and that merge in origin/main. Version boundary: dbf67daef2c624c1d5f01ef4233a8bccb3c927aa is contained by tags v0.1.2, v0.2.0, and v0.3.0, while no tag contains d94dedb56cec78461cd14113c337034734813d58 or 997009a6778687ac8c1f0833f2850ea808742cce. RubyGems lists released 0.1.0, 0.1.2, 0.2.0, and 0.3.0; current lib/upright/version.rb remains 0.3.0 and CHANGELOG.md records CVE-2026-67990 under Unreleased. Thus every published gem version is vulnerable and the fix exists only on unreleased history as of the audit.
reasoning: The vulnerable behavior is the combination of ambient session authentication, an explicit global CSRF skip on each metrics proxy, and unrestricted forwarding to upstream APIs; the advisory's cited snapshot demonstrates that complete attack path. Line-level history does not support treating the January public addition as causal authorship: both controllers arrive already formed in a commit whose stated operation is a move during a repository extraction, and the next commit only changes Ruby namespace syntax. The public parent lacks the files, but the root and first-party project history establish that this is a boundary created by open-sourcing an existing internal tool, not proof that dbf67daef2c624c1d5f01ef4233a8bccb3c927aa first wrote the flawed mechanism. Protocol therefore forbids selecting that move as the BIC. The remediation was developed as a sequence because the first provenance gate still allowed residual cases; d94dedb56cec78461cd14113c337034734813d58 is the final direct CSRF implementation whose relevant tree landed through 997009a6778687ac8c1f0833f2850ea808742cce. All release tags precede that landing, matching the Unreleased changelog and the advisory's absence of a released version range. Since the true BIC and its commit object are outside accessible public history, neither immediate-parent absence for the original write nor BIC-only AI authorship can be established. This is a genuine public-history boundary, so BLOCKED is required rather than NOT_AI or EVIDENCE_GAP.
remaining_gap: The inaccessible pre-open-source/internal Git commit that first wrote the two session-authenticated proxy controllers with skip_forgery_protection, its immediate parent tree, and that BIC commit object's author/committer/trailers are required to complete causal and AI attribution; the public extraction begins after those facts already existed. No patched gem release is available yet, although the fix is present on origin/main.
